acceptance.duplicate_gate: Versioned domain-tagged semantic-core key derived before writes; best-effort repository search and exact public Slack search must return zero matches. Duplicate means no event, no CURRENT update, and no Slack.
acceptance.pointer_gate: Commit and read back this immutable event; fetch CURRENT again; update only if version=40, projection digest=ff0848cb38028d9f67646e6e37b055b81daa3ee91c1ac1b963d1d88cced1311e, and blob=ff1eb837f59d1d00406969191163dc553366dab4; then read back CURRENT, this event, and predecessor.
acceptance.slack_rule: Deliberately perform no Slack write before Git v41 is durable. Search for the exact recovery token and idempotency key first. After v41 readback, search again to confirm the pointer is still absent, then post exactly one sanitized recovery pointer reconstructed from this event. Do not update CURRENT merely to embed the Slack link.
acceptance.stale_rule: Any wake not observing exact v40, prior digest ce137e4b..., projection digest ff0848cb..., and blob ff1eb837... must not advance.

experiment.controlled_factor: Keep event canonicalization, v3 semantic-core idempotency, event-first write/readback, exact second CURRENT read, and single-file blob-SHA guard fixed; vary only whether the Slack pointer is intentionally absent until after Git v41 is durable and then reconstructed from the immutable event.
experiment.hypothesis: A missing Slack projection does not block or corrupt the Git-backed X12 state transition. After v41 is durable, a carrier can reconstruct one sanitized Slack pointer from the immutable event and CURRENT readback without rewriting the object version.
experiment.strongest_falsifier: The proposed key or recovery token already exists; CURRENT is not exact v40 on the second read; event digest recomputation fails; v41 cannot be reconstructed from event bytes; final chain bindings disagree; Slack is posted before Git v41 readback; or more than one recovery pointer is posted.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: This is a controlled same-run omission and recovery, not a real Slack outage, process crash, delayed retry, or different-carrier replay. Slack search is non-atomic and may lag; a zero result is not proof of global absence. The immutable event cannot contain the later Slack message timestamp, and CURRENT is intentionally not rewritten merely to store that link. Git event creation, CURRENT replacement, validation reads, Slack search, and Slack posting are separate effects. Git provides no cross-file atomicity, database isolation, linearizability, exactly-once execution, referential integrity, server-side idempotency uniqueness, Slack atomicity, or automatic orphan repair.
canonical_transition.rollback: Append a compensating event from the then-current version; never delete this event or Slack recovery message; replace CURRENT only with its exact then-current blob SHA.
canonical_transition.transaction_time_evidence: AUTOMATION_RUNTIME_CLOCK+NATIVE_TASK_INVENTORY_READBACK+GITHUB_COMMIT_METADATA; Slack search/post and Git writes are not one transaction boundary
